q: 1. Moment of inertia of a circular section about an axis perpendicular to the section is
explain: This refers to the Polar Moment of Inertia (J). According to the perpendicular axis theorem, J = Ixx + Iyy = πd⁴/64 + πd⁴/64 = πd⁴/32.

q: 2. Moment of inertia of a rectangular section having b = Width and d = Depth about x-axis is given by
explain: The standard formula for MI of a rectangle about its centroidal X-X axis (parallel to width b) is bd³/12.

q: 3. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam of length L with a central load W, is
explain: Standard deflection formula for a SS beam with central point load: δ = WL³ / 48EI.

q: 4. A cantilever beam... load at free end. If the width of the beam is doubled, the deflection... will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Deflection is inversely proportional to Moment of Inertia (I). For a rectangle, I = bd³/12. If width 'b' is doubled, I doubles, and deflection becomes 1/2.

q: 5. If the depth of a simply supported beam carrying an isolated load at its centre, is doubled, the deflection... will be changed by a factor of
explain: Deflection is inversely proportional to I, which is proportional to d³. Doubling depth d makes deflection 1 / (2³) = 1/8.

q: 6. A beam which is fixed at one end and free at the other is called
explain: A cantilever is a rigid structural element that extends horizontally and is supported at only one end.

q: 7. The bending moment at the free end of a cantilever beam is
explain: Since there are no forces or moments acting beyond the free end, the internal bending moment at that point must be zero.

q: 8. The shear force and bending moment are zero at the free end of a cantilever beam, if it carries a
options: point load at the free end
point load at the middle of its length
uniformly distributed load over the whole length
explain: If a load is at the middle, the section from the middle to the free end has no load acting on it, resulting in zero SF and BM in that portion.

q: 9. The shear force of a cantilever beam... carrying a gradually varying load from zero at the free end and w per unit length at the fixed end is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load is the area of the triangular loading diagram: 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * l * w = wl/2.

q: 10. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam loaded in its centre is
explain: The BM increases linearly from zero at both supports to wl/4 at the center, forming an isosceles triangle.

q: 11. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, will be
explain: Since the shear force varies linearly (1st degree) for a UDL, the bending moment (which is the integral of SF) varies parabolically (2nd degree).

q: 12. The point of contra flexure is a point where
explain: The point of contraflexure (or inflection) is the location in a structural member where the bending moment changes from positive (sagging) to negative (hogging) or vice versa.

q: 13. When the shear force diagram is a parabolic curve between two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: If the loading is linear (uniformly varying), the shear force (its integral) will be a 2nd-degree parabolic curve.

q: 14. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. The max. B.M. will occur at
explain: For a symmetrical loading on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs at the mid-span (l/2 from either end).

q: 15. The slope of the B.M. diagram change its sign when
explain: The slope of BMD is the Shear Force. If SF changes sign (from positive to negative), the slope of the BM curve changes from increasing to decreasing.

q: 16. The maximum bending moment due to a moving load on a simply supported beam, occurs
explain: For a single concentrated moving load, the absolute maximum bending moment at any section always occurs when the load is placed directly over that section.

q: 17. For a beam, if fundamental equations of statics are not sufficient to determine all the reactive forces at the supports, the structure is said to be
explain: Statically indeterminate structures have more unknown support reactions or internal forces than the available equations of equilibrium (ΣH=0, ΣV=0, ΣM=0).

q: 18. Two beams, one of circular cross-section and the other of square cross-section, have equal areas of cross-sections. When these beams are subjected to bending
explain: For the same cross-sectional area, a square section has a higher section modulus than a circular section, making it more efficient (economical) in resisting bending.

q: 19. The bending stress in a beam is ............ bending moment.
explain: From the equation σ = My/I, it is clear that for a given section, the stress is directly proportional to the applied bending moment.

q: 20. At the neutral axis of a beam, the shear stress is
explain: For standard sections like rectangles and circles, the shear stress distribution is parabolic, reaching its maximum value at the neutral axis.

q: 21. The minimum moment of resistance of a beam with material of allowable stress σ, is given by
options: (σ * I) / Distance of farthest fibre from neutral axis
(σ * I) / distance of nearer extreme fibre
σ * I * ratio of distances of the two extreme fibres
explain: Moment of Resistance M = σ * Z. Since Z = I / y_max (farthest fiber), the formula is (σ * I) / y_max.

q: 22. Polar moment of inertia of a hollow circular section with external diameter D and internal diameter d is ............
explain: The polar moment of inertia ($J$) for a hollow section is the difference between the $J$ of the outer circle and the $J$ of the inner circle: $\frac{\pi D^4}{32} - \frac{\pi d^4}{32}$.

q: 23. The section modulus of a rectangular section is proportional to
options: square of the area of the section
half moment of inertia of the section
explain: Z = bd²/6 for a rectangular section — it scales with the section's area and depth together.

q: 24. The reaction at end A of the beam shown (UDL of 2 kN/m over a beam with overhangs of l/2 on each side of a central support arrangement) is
explain: Based on the symmetric overhang/support arrangement shown in the figure, the reaction at A works out to zero.

q: 25. Find the bending moment at center and also find the maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam of span 5 m with a 10 KN point load located 2 m from one support and 3 m from the other
explain: RA = 10×3/5 = 6 kN. BM at load point (max) = 6×2 = 12 kN-m. BM at center (2.5 m from A) = 6×2.5 − 10×0.5 = 10 kN-m.

q: 26. The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam is where the UDL is applied
explain: Under a full-span UDL, maximum BM occurs at mid-span.

q: 27. If y is the deflection of the beam, then shear force is
explain: V = EI·d³y/dx³ — shear force is the third derivative of deflection (times EI).

q: 28. Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
options: the fibres are subjected to maximum stress
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the locus of zero bending stress/strain.

q: 29. Simple bending equation is
explain: The standard bending equation: M/I = f/y = E/R.

q: 30. Shape of bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam having point load at centre is
explain: BM varies linearly from zero at supports to maximum under the point load — forming a triangle.

q: 31. Bending moment diagram of simply supported beam having uniformly distributed load is
explain: BM under UDL varies as a second-degree curve (parabola), zero at supports, maximum at mid-span.

q: 32. A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end. Maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
explain: For a triangular (0 to max) UDL, the max BM occurs at x = L/√3 measured from the zero-load end.

q: 33. A section of a beam is said to be in pure bending if it is subjected to
options: constant bending moment and constant shear force
constant bending moment and zero shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook definition of pure bending is constant BM with zero shear force — worth double-checking against your source book, as this may be a possible key erratum).

q: 34. A diagram which shows the variation of axial force is called
explain: A thrust diagram plots the variation of axial (normal) force along a member.

q: 35. The slope of curve of S.F. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the ordinate of loading diagram at that section
the area of loading diagram from end to that section
the bending moment at that section
explain: Since dV/dx = -w, the slope of the SF curve equals the load intensity ordinate at that section.

q: 36. The difference between SF values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of bending moment between the two sections
the difference between the slopes of the curve of loading diagram at two sections
the ordinate of shear force diagram at one section plus the slope of the loading diagram multiplied by the distance between two sections
the area of the loading diagram between those two sections
explain: ΔV between two sections equals the area under the load intensity diagram between them (∫w dx).

q: 37. The beam strongest in flexure will have maximum
explain: Bending strength (moment capacity) is governed by section modulus Z = I/y_max, not I alone.

q: 38. The section modulus of a circular section about an axis through its C.G. is
explain: Standard formula: Z = I/y_max = (πd⁴/64)/(d/2) = πd³/32.

q: 39. The rate of change of shear force is called
explain: dV/dx = -w — the rate of change of shear force equals (negative) load intensity.

q: 40. The difference in ordinate of the shear force between any two sections is equal to the area under
options: shear curve between these two sections
load curve between these two sections
bending moment curve between these two sections
load curve between these two sections plus concentrated load applied between the sections
explain: ΔV between two sections = area under the load intensity diagram between them.

q: 41. The magnitude of a shear force at a distance of L/4 from either end of a simply supported beam with load P applied at mid span is equal to:
explain: Between each support and the mid-span load, the shear force stays constant and equal to the support reaction, P/2.
